en:
...The seventh one wasn't coming.
Waiting any longer would only be a waste of time.
The six who had come for me were fidgeting too, clearly wanting to go home.
...But I couldn't shake this uneasy feeling in my chest.
What was this foreboding?
I couldn't shake the sense that something was about to happen.
Would it be something good...
Or something bad...?
Everyone's eyes gathered on me.
All the stories were over.
Everyone was waiting for me to speak.{p}What should I do?
Suggest we all go home
Suggest we wait a little longer

"...Um.
Everyone, thank you so much for today.
It's a shame the seventh person didn't come, but I got to hear some really scary stories, so I think I can write a good article.
It's getting late, and I hate to ask, but...
Um, everyone, could you possibly spare me a little more of your time?"
I couldn't find the right words.
How could I explain this uneasy feeling?
Everyone listened to me, looking surprised.{p}

"...Why should we have to stay?
Do you have some lead on the seventh one, then?
If not, I'd rather you didn't tie me down.
I don't belong to you, after all."
It was Iwashita.
Keeping her head down, she glared up at me from under her brows.
Her eyes were so defiant that they overpowered me.{p}

...The mood had turned ugly.
Maybe I shouldn't have said that.
What should I do?{p}Should I put it differently?
Let's go home after all
Sorry. Please stay a while longer

"I'm sorry.
Could you please stay here, even just a little longer?"{p}

"Why?"
It was Shindo.
"What's the reason?
The seventh one isn't coming. Our stories are done.
You shouldn't need us anymore.
So why do we have to stick around?
Give me a reason."
Shindo seemed a little ticked off, too.
"...There's no reason.
I just have this strange, uneasy feeling.
Like, for some reason, we have to stay here..."{p}

"This is pointless, you know.
Unlike you, I happen to be a busy man.
I'll be taking my leave."
It was Kazama who cut in, instead of Shindo.{p}

Kazama was right.
I couldn't keep everyone here with no clear reason, just because of my own uneasy feeling.{p}

"See ya. So long."
Shindo got up from his seat.{p}

"...Sorry, {a}.
I'm going home too."
Then Fukuzawa, too.
After her, Kazama and Iwashita got up as well.{p}

Only Hosoda and Arai stayed in their seats, watching me.
Did these two feel the same unease I did?{p}
"See ya."
Shindo said it once more and opened the club room door.{p}

"Whoa!"
Shindo suddenly jumped.{p}

"Sanae!"
The moment Fukuzawa saw the girl standing there, blocking the doorway, she poked her head out from behind Shindo.{p}
...Sanae?{p}Sanae... Wasn't she...
I remember Sanae
Who's Sanae?

Sanae... Was she that strange girl Fukuzawa had told us about?
The strange girl who supposedly had old men and old women living inside her body, telling her about tests and things that were going to happen.
Why was she here...?
Don't tell me she was the seventh one?{p}

She didn't answer Fukuzawa. Instead, she looked around at each of us in turn, as if sizing us up.
And the moment her eyes met mine, she froze completely.
"...Are you {a}?"
She gave off a really strange impression.
Maybe Fukuzawa had been right about her.
...What should I do?{p}Should I just admit it?
Answer yes
Answer no

"...Uh, yes."
I hesitated a little, but decided to answer honestly.{p}

Then her eyes traveled over me, from the top of my head to the tips of my toes.
"Huh?"
For a moment, what she meant didn't sink in.
"Don't go home!"
Did she have eyes in the back of her head?
She suddenly spun around and sharply called out to Shindo, who was about to walk out the door.
Shindo turned around with a puzzled look, but grudgingly drew back the foot he had stepped out with.{p}

"Hey, look.
I'm going home now.
Unless you're the seventh one and you're gonna tell us the last story, that is."
He seemed pretty irritated at being sassed by a first-year like her.
"I'm not the seventh one."
"Then I'm leaving."
"If you leave now, you'll die."{p}

She said something that dangerous without batting an eye.
That was enough to stop Shindo in his tracks.
"I'm gonna die...?
Keep up the sick jokes and I'm gonna get mad for real."
No matter how Shindo tried to intimidate her, she kept talking back, perfectly calm.{p}

"Yes, they're coming.
To kill someone in this room."
Then she looked at me and smiled sweetly.
...Someone's going to be killed?
Hold on a minute.
Please don't say things like that with a smile.
"Oh, Reiko!"
When she spotted Fukuzawa, she went over to her, and they clasped hands.
Fukuzawa had already called out to her. Had she really not noticed her until now?
"Wow, you're here too, Reiko.
Good for you, not getting killed."{p}

"Geez, Sanae, you're always like this.
Didn't you notice me waving at you?"
"I didn't notice.
Grandma didn't tell me about that."
...The two of them were having a conversation that made no sense to me.
I didn't think I could keep up with them.{p}

"...Would you two move?
Dying, being killed, none of it has anything to do with me.
I'll be going home now."
With that, Iwashita pushed her way between the two of them.{p}
"You're going to die, you know."{p}

"Me?
Heh heh... You're saying I'll be killed?
If anyone like that exists, I'll kill them first, before I ever die.
Instead of worrying about other people, you should worry about yourself."
Iwashita's face was smiling, but her eyes were terribly cold.{p}

Then she pushed Iwashita back as she tried to leave, and shut the club room door.
"Everyone, please go back to your seats."
There was a strange force about her.
Fukuzawa sat back down right away.
Kazama threw up his hands and tilted his head, as if to say "I can't believe this," then sighed and went back to the seat he'd been sitting in.
Shindo and Iwashita went back to their seats in sullen silence.
And once she had made sure everyone was seated, Sanae... I mean, Motoki sat down in the seat that had been set out for the seventh person.{p}

"I'll tell the last story.
{a}, is that okay?"
Motoki asked for my approval.{p}What should I do?
Please go ahead
No, if the seventh one is coming, let's wait
"Oh, please go ah..."{p}

"Wait a sec."
It was Fukuzawa who stopped me mid-sentence.
"Hey, Sanae.
There's something I want to ask you first.
Did I ever tell you about this meeting today?"{p}

Motoki quietly shook her head.
"Nuh-uh.
But Grandma told me.
She said if I didn't hurry over, something terrible would happen."
...Motoki really was unhinged.
Her eyes had a faraway, crazed look.
Should I really go on and listen to her story?{p}

...Could it be that the uneasy feeling I'd had was about Motoki?
Had she seen right through what I was thinking?{p}
Suddenly, she stared hard at my face.{p}

"Oh, that's right.
{a}, I forgot to tell you something important.
The reason I came here was to save you.
{a}, you and I are going to get married, apparently.
So Grandma told me to go save you.
If you die, I'll never be able to get married my whole life."
What★
Me, marry this girl?
Grandma said so?
...Maybe I should have gone home after all.{p}

...Oh no. Kazama and Shindo were both looking at me with big grins.
That was a far cry from the sulky faces they'd had a minute ago, but...{p}
What did telling the seventh story have to do with saving me?{p}What was I supposed to say to that?
Say "I'll marry you" from the bottom of my heart
Say "I'll marry you," even if it's a lie
Say I can't promise something like that

...I couldn't hurt Motoki's feelings in front of everyone.
Besides, if what she said was true, she had gone out of her way and taken a risk to come here for my sake.
She was a little unhinged, but wasn't that part of her charm, too?
...And it wasn't as if we were getting married right now.
If there really was a red thread of fate in this world, maybe a meeting like this wasn't so bad.
I made up my mind.{p}
When I said that, a cheer went up all around me.{p}

"Wow, way to go, {a}!
You're marrying Sanae!
You'd better invite me to the wedding!"
Fukuzawa was cackling.{p}

"Wow, I sure got to see something amazing.
I came here thinking I'd be telling scary stories, but somehow I got to see something really nice you hardly ever get to see.
Oh, jeez..."
Hosoda scratched his head, blushing.
It was as if he thought he was the one who'd gotten a love confession.{p}

"It's good to settle your life early.
For a commoner like you, planning your life out early is vital.
I'll be rooting for you, too.
You make a fine couple, ah ha ha ha ha..."
Kazama was saying whatever he pleased, since it was no concern of his.{p}

Shindo just kept smirking.
Iwashita and Arai kept their heads down, looking uninterested.{p}

...Nice to meet you, everyone.
You might already know about me from Reiko's story, but I'll introduce myself anyway.
My name is Sanae Motoki, and I'm a first-year.
I'll tell the last story before the seventh one comes.
This is a story I heard from my grandma.{p}

My grandma lives inside me, and she knows all kinds of things.
Sometimes she slips out of my body.
And then she goes and sees all sorts of stuff.
This is something that grandma saw.
It happened just recently.{p}

There was a student at this school named Takuro Kanda.
Kanda had a girlfriend.
She was super jealous.
So she kept Kanda on a tight leash.
She'd call him every night to check if he was home, and grill him about everything he'd done that day.
If a girl so much as came near him, she'd question him over and over, or throw a hysterical fit and get insanely angry.
Kanda got scared of her.
And he started wanting to break up with her.{p}

Right around then, a girl showed up who said she liked Kanda.
And that girl started getting close to Kanda.
Of course, when the jealous girlfriend found out, she got really, really angry.
But Kanda started going out with the girl behind her back anyway.{p}

But, see, there was someone who had a one-sided crush on that girl.
He hated Kanda's guts.
...A few days after that, Kanda died.
He died on the train tracks.
He used the rail as a pillow, took sleeping pills, and fell asleep right there.
Then a train came along, and its wheels ran over his head, and he died.
His head was crushed to a pulp, so badly they couldn't put it back together.
It was written off as suicide, but nobody knows if that's the truth.{p}

"That was booooring!"
The moment Motoki's story ended, Shindo was the one who yelled it.
Iwashita scoffed.
...True, compared with the stories I'd heard so far, it didn't really have much of a point, and I couldn't call it interesting by any means.
...Then again, compared with Kazama's story, it was plenty scary.
But what did that story have to do with me being saved?
Maybe I'd been taken in by one of Motoki's jokes.{p}

"Hey, {a}."
Motoki took my hand as I sat there spacing out, and suddenly squeezed it tight.
I turned bright red.
"...Hey, {a}.
Do you think Kanda's death was a suicide?
Or do you think someone killed him?
If someone did kill him, who do you think it was?"
Why was Motoki asking me something like that?{p}What was the point of asking that?
Suicide
His hysterical girlfriend killed him
The girl who secretly loved Kanda
The guy with a one-sided crush on that girl
Someone else

"I see.
So that's what you think, {a}.
...It doesn't really mean anything.
My grandma won't tell me who killed him either.
Maybe she really doesn't know.
But you know, the seventh one is coming soon.
Who do you think the seventh one is?
...That's right, it's Kanda. Kanda is coming here."{p}

Shindo looked a little uncomfortable.
"...Well, sure, it's not like I didn't know him.
He was in my class.
But I only knew him a little.
If it's Kanda you wanna know about, wouldn't Iwashita know more than me?
There was a rumor Iwashita was going out with Kanda."{p}

What?
My heart skipped, and I found myself turning to look at Iwashita.
Iwashita was smiling, her head bowed.
...Had I just said something terrible?
If Shindo was right, I'd just said that Iwashita killed Kanda.
And I'd even called her someone who might do anything...
I wondered if I had offended Iwashita.
"...Well, who knows?
And Shindo, I don't think you should be so quick to believe rumors about people.{p}

Did you see it?
Did you see something going on between Kanda and me?
You didn't see a thing, so for your own good, you'd better not spread strange rumors.
I can't stand liars, you know.
If I really had been going out with a man named Kanda, I'm sure I would have wanted to kill him.{p}

...More to the point, your name was Fukuzawa, wasn't it?
I hear you secretly had feelings for Kanda.
And I heard that Kanda had recently started going out with a new girl.
Though, of course, that's nothing more than a rumor either.
I believe her name was Reiko Fukuzawa..."{p}

"What are you talking about?!"
Cutting Iwashita off, Fukuzawa slammed her hand down on the desk.
"Senior or not, there are things you just don't say!
Are you saying I killed Kanda?
Sure, I'll admit I liked him.
But why would I have to kill him?
When he died, I was the one who grieved the most!
I know the truth!
It was YOU!
You're the one who killed him!"{p}

I could only stare, stunned.
Fukuzawa was glaring at Iwashita with a terrifying look on her face.{p}
But Iwashita, meeting that glare, wasn't backing down either.{p}

"...Proof?
If you say I killed him, then go on, show me the proof.
Say one careless word, and I wouldn't mind killing you."
The two of them kept glaring at each other.
I had no idea what to do.{p}

It was Hosoda who stepped in between them.
"Now, now, please don't get so angry, you two.
Everyone, let's stop imagining weird things.
Whoever killed him, it has nothing to do with us here, does it?
What good is arguing about it going to do?
Let's all get along.
Okay?"
The two of them didn't pay the slightest attention to Hosoda.
They kept glaring at each other in silence.
Just then, Arai cleared his throat.{p}

"Ahem.
I don't know much about that story, but it sounds rather complicated.
...Hosoda, you like Fukuzawa, don't you?
That's only a guess, of course.
Ever since you got here, you've been sneaking glances at Fukuzawa, haven't you?
Is there something going on?"
Arai looked at Hosoda with probing eyes.{p}

"Ah ha ha ha, so you caught me, huh?
Truth is, I've been watching Fukuzawa this whole time, thinking a girl just my type had joined the first-years.
It's a one-sided crush, though...
I never dreamed I'd get to sit and talk with her like this today.
Oh, this is so embarrassing."
Hosoda bent his big body double, shaking with stifled laughter.{p}

Kazama got up from his seat.
"...How ridiculous.
Every one of you is connected to Kanda, one way or another.
This is a trap Hino set up, isn't it?
He was close with Kanda, after all.
I can't go along with this farce any longer.
I'm going home.
The rest of you can play detective all you like."
Just as Kazama's hand closed on the doorknob...{p}

"Wait!"
Motoki cried out.
"I told you the seventh one is coming, didn't I?
You can't go home before then."{p}

Hearing Motoki, Kazama let out an exaggerated sigh.
"Haaaaaah.
Look, what exactly am I to you?
We only met today, didn't we?
Your grandma living inside your body, hearing your grandpa's voice... You're seriously unhinged, you know.
I'm a busy man.
I'm not like you common folk.
Sorry, but I'm going to do as I please."{p}

"No!
If you open the door now, you'll be killed.
Kanda is already here.
He's standing right on the other side of that door."
Motoki warned him sharply and pointed at the club room door.
At her words, Kazama turned to look at the door.
He furrowed his brow and strained his eyes, as if trying to see right through to the other side.{p}

...But that was absurd.
No matter what, there was no way a dead person would just come strolling into a place like this.{p}

"Hey, {a}.
Do you believe what I'm telling you?
Or do you think I'm a weird girl after all?"{p}Motoki suddenly asked me that.
I believe you
Come on, that's too much. I can't believe that
Let's rethink getting married after all. You're not normal

"...I believe you."
Now all I could do was believe what Motoki said.
The ominous air I'd felt ever since I entered this room wasn't just my imagination.
It had to be a sign that something was coming.
Motoki smiled at me, looking truly happy.{p}

At some point, Kazama had gone back to his seat too.
It seemed that even he didn't have the nerve to open the door.{p}

"He's there. I knew it.
Kanda is right outside the club room door.
Grandma told me so.
She says Kanda can't pass on unless he kills someone, anyone at all.
She says he has to take someone's head, the same way his was taken."
Motoki murmured quietly.
Everyone fell silent.{p}

Motoki went on.
"...The person who killed Kanda is one of us here.
What reason they had, why they had to kill him, I won't press for that.
But I think that person should be the one sacrificed. I don't know who it is, though."{p}

"You've gotta be kidding me!
I'm going home!"
Kazama stood up.
Then he ran over to the window.{p}

"...What the hell?!
The window won't open!
Fine, I'll smash this damn window!"
As Kazama grabbed a chair to hurl it at the window, Motoki spoke to him, perfectly calm.{p}

"...Nothing you do will work.
This room has been cursed by Kanda.
It's completely sealed.
There's no way out.
Until one of us dies, we can never leave this room."{p}

...Iwashita just glared at one spot on the door and answered without so much as a glance at Shindo.
"...Proof?
Do you have proof that I killed him?
Keep saying whatever you like with no proof, and I'll kill you."{p}

Fukuzawa didn't keep quiet either.
"You!
You're the one who killed my Kanda!
You said you liked me, so you were against Kanda and me going out.
That's why you hated him and killed him!
Take responsibility!"
The one Fukuzawa was hurling abuse at was Hosoda.{p}

Hosoda looked lost, on the verge of tears.
"...Fukuzawa, please don't say that.
You were never supposed to fall for a guy like Kanda.
You're my goddess.
I'm not saying I want to go out with you or anything like that, Fukuzawa.
Just looking at you is enough for me.
Just watching you from far away and imagining makes me happy, you know."
At last, Hosoda burst into tears.{p}
...What on earth was this? What was with these people?{p}

"...See? Kanda's angry.
What are you going to do?
If this keeps up, Kanda's going to come into the club room.

And then he'll kill every one of us."
By the time Motoki said that, it was already too late.{p}

The door was blown away by some supernatural force, and a man was standing there.
...It was probably Kanda.
I could only say 'probably' partly because I had never known Kanda, but more than that, because there was nothing above his neck.
A headless man in a school uniform stood there.{p}

"It wasn't me!
I'm sorry I made a move on Iwashita!
But I'm not the one who killed you, right?"
Kazama threw himself to the floor in an abject kowtow and begged for forgiveness.{p}

"I-I didn't do anything wrong.
What I did to you was just a little prank.
I never meant to bully you.
...Th-that was just a bit of fun!"
Shindo shrank back, ready to run, and apologized desperately in a trembling voice.{p}

"...K-Kanda.
It was just a little joke.
Iwashita kept flaunting what she had with you, so I just wanted to steal you away from her.
I wasn't planning to dump you or anything.
I'm sorry, I'm sorry... Please don't kill me!"
Fukuzawa's face was crumpled, her palms pressed together in prayer.{p}

"...Y-you know it wasn't me, right?
I-I have nothing to do with it.
Sure, I hated you for stealing Fukuzawa, so I pushed you down the stairs and put thumbtacks in your shoes, but nobody dies from stuff like that, right?
It wasn't me."
Hosoda was squeezing himself into a corner of the room, trying to get even a little farther away.{p}
...Arai said nothing, made no attempt to run, and just sat there without moving, his head bowed.{p}

"...You deserved to be killed.
Anyone at all could have done it.
I imagine everyone wanted to kill you, don't you think?
Do you hate me?
Do you think I killed you?
...Then why don't you kill me?"
Iwashita didn't try to run either. She stayed in her chair and glared at Kanda.{p}

...Even so, apart from Arai, the only one keeping silent, any one of them could have killed Kanda.
Even if Kanda's death had been a suicide, something one of them did could easily have been what drove him to it.{p}

Just then, a strange voice echoed inside my head.
I knew by instinct that it was Kanda's voice.
(...Who should I kill?
Who do I have to kill to be saved?
...One of the people here.
You decide.)
I looked around the club room.{p}

It seemed I was the only one who could hear that voice.
The voice pressed me to choose.
I had to make one of these people the victim.{p}What should I do?!
Akemi Iwashita
Nozomu Kazama
Makoto Shindo
Tomoharu Hosoda
Shoji Arai
Reiko Fukuzawa
Myself
Sanae Motoki

...Every one of them seemed like the killer.
...But there was no solid proof.
Besides, even if one of them was the killer, there was no way they'd admit to it.
But if this went on, we would all be killed.
...I couldn't possibly choose just one person.
In that instant, the name that came into my head was my own.
I steeled myself and took one step toward Kanda.{p}

Just then,
Motoki, who had been holding my hand, began to shake violently.{p}

Suddenly, something like white smoke came out of her mouth.
In the smoke, the face of a woman with a horrifying expression appeared.
The instant it appeared, it lunged at Kanda.
The vengeful spirit's bitter groan thundered through the club room.{p}

...And then the thing was gone.
The headless man in the school uniform vanished like an illusion.{p}
And once it had seen that happen, the demonic face floating in the smoke turned into a very calm, gentle face, and slid smoothly back into Motoki's mouth.{p}
...I felt as if I were dreaming.{p}

"Motoki!
...Sanae!"
I caught her as she crumpled.
Then I shook her by the shoulders.{p}

She let out a sleepy murmur and slowly opened her eyes.
"...Grandma says everything's okay now.
Isn't it great? Nobody died."
She was smiling.
I nodded hard.
It was all over.{p}

...After that, a week went by.
I never saw any of them again after that day.
In the end, I never found out who killed Kanda, or even whether it had been a suicide or a murder in the first place.
...Every human being has evil in their heart.
What holds it in check is self-control.{p}

But sometimes, finding the slightest gap in our self-control, the evil in our hearts shows itself.
...In the end, I can't blame anyone.
Whatever really happened between Kanda and whoever it was.
It's not my job to pursue it.
If they feel the pangs of a human conscience, then all that's left is for them to atone for their sins themselves.{p}

"Heeey, {a}!"
...Oh, it's Sanae.
Sanae came running toward me, waving.{p}
I looked at my watch.

She was right on time.
Ever since that day, Sanae and I have talked a lot.
I think she's an honest, good girl.
I don't completely believe her stories about the grandma and grandpa who supposedly live inside her, but I'm sure she really does have some strange power.
And meeting her has made me believe in fate, in something that can't be written off as coincidence.{p}

Whether Sanae and I will really get married someday, I can't know yet; that's still a long way off.
But for now, I want to take good care of her.{p}

...Come to think of it, yesterday I finished the manuscript for the special feature on the school's seven wonders.
I agonized over what to do about the seventh story, but there was no way I could write about what happened in the club room.
So instead, I wrote: 'Something bad happens to whoever hears the seventh story. That is why it cannot be written here.'
If you hear all of a school's seven wonders, something bad will happen...
It seems every school has a rumor like that.
I don't think I'll ever tell anyone about what happened that day...{p}

"Everyone, thank you so much for today.
It's a shame the seventh person never came, but I got to hear some really scary stories, so I think I can write a good article.
It's late, so please be careful on your way home..."
I bowed deeply to everyone.{p}

"Took forever, but hey, it was fun."
That was Shindo.{p}

"See ya."
Shindo was the first to open the club room door.{p}

"You're right.
I really can't keep you all here any longer.
It's late, too.
This uneasy feeling must just be my imagination.
Sorry for all the trouble, everyone.
Please be careful on your way home."
I said it with my head down.
But my bad feeling didn't go away; it only grew stronger and stronger.
In that atmosphere, everyone was starting to get ready to leave.{p}

"See ya."
Shindo was the first to open the club room door.{p}

...Um, who's Sanae?
Is she someone I know?
Have I met her somewhere?
She looks like a student at this school, but there are so many of us.
I'm sure I've seen her at least once.
...I can't remember.
Could she be the seventh one?
Ignoring Fukuzawa, she looked around at each of us in turn, as if sizing us up.
And the moment she looked me in the eye, she froze.{p}

"...Are you {a}?"
How does this girl know who I am?
What is it about her... she has a really mysterious air.
Then she looked at my face and smiled sweetly.{p}

"Ah!"
I cried out without meaning to.
For an instant, I thought something squirmed inside her mouth.
Was it my imagination?
...That's it!
It hit me.
This scene rings a bell.
Yes, she's Sanae Motoki, the girl from Fukuzawa's story.
That's why she gave me such a strange impression.{p}

"...Uh, no."
That's what I found myself answering.
"Why would you lie like that?
I know perfectly well that you're {a}."
Motoki said to me.
Why did I lie?
It's not as if I'd done anything shameful that I'd need to lie to her about.
I apologized to her.
"...Sorry, I didn't mean to lie.
Yes, I'm {b} {a}."
She came closer to me.{p}

"No, that doesn't matter.
But I'm so glad you're alive."{p}

Just then, Arai cut in.
"Why not?
We could wait here forever and get nowhere...
In that case, I think we may as well hear her story.
It makes no difference who tells the seventh story."{p}

He might have a point.
If we unexpectedly get to hear an interesting story out of this, that's a bonus.
But she's a girl with a dangerous air about her. Will it be all right?
Is it really okay to leave the seventh story to someone like that?
Hope and anxiety mingled inside me.{p}

...I can't hurt Motoki in front of everyone.
If I just say this for now, I can always talk my way out of it later.
Motoki gives off a slightly dangerous vibe, but looking at her like this, she's actually pretty cute.
Even if we did end up going out, it might work out pretty well.
For now, I'll let her save face.{p}
"Yeah, all right. If you'll have me."{p}

"Motoki.
